summary: Original frozen candidate: two recovery-marker ownership defects and one integration-test gap. Callback fencing, cumulative acknowledgement and drain ownership otherwise appear coherent; no additional lost-wake counterexample found.

findings.claim: Successful receipt persistence can clear an unacknowledged previous-crash marker: shutdown or a paused settings change starts the startup-gap drain, whose endSafetyWork clears the marker despite requiresRecoveryConfirmation remaining true. Next launch loses the Safety Pause reason.
findings.recommendation: Separate prior-launch recovery ownership from live work. Test preseeded interruption markers surviving successful shutdown drains and paused settings changes until explicit resume.

findings.claim: Resume while recovery-paused receipt persistence is running clears the live-work marker. Further overlapping beginSafetyWork calls do not restore it because safetyWorkCount is already nonzero.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledge prior interruption while retaining live/pending ownership. Gate persistence, resume, and assert the marker remains until current work finishes.

findings.claim: The eight tests do not exercise actual shared persistenceTask reentry when B arrives during A persistence, or partial multi-root failure. Manual mailbox acknowledgements prove the revision rule, not probe/controller integration.
findings.recommendation: Gate actual invalidation after A capture, admit same-time B, reject stale acknowledgement and publication; fail root two, retain cumulative roots, then retry both. Exercise the controller callback/drain route too.
